title: Slice-and-Serve CAIQ: per-section signed attestation modules & pay-per-section pricing pilot
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Problem: Sales and legal teams frequently request subsets of SIG/CAIQ answers (e.g., infrastructure, auth, data residency) for proof-of-compliance during negotiations. Full CAIQ bundles are heavy and create evidence bloat, increasing turnaround time and legal effort.

Motivation: Reduce friction for mid-market and enterprise contract cycles by enabling on-demand, signed per-section attestations that are cryptographically anchored to a canonical CAIQ record. This enables sales to pull only the sections customers need, pay for narrowly scoped evidence, and receive a verifiable signed artifact for SOC/contract review.

Proposal: Build a "slice-and-serve" attestation flow: 1) author canonical CAIQ answers in the existing Confluence/Answers repo; 2) allow PM/Legal to mark sections as "sliceable"; 3) generate per-section signed attestation modules (PDF + machine-readable JSON) that include a CAIQ canonical-hash and signature from Redwood's attestation service; 4) surface a pay-per-section pricing option in the Sales Portal and Attestation Console with an audit trail.

Success metrics: reduce time-to-deliver attestation snippets from 2 days -> <4 hours for standard slices; increase self-serve attestation conversions for mid-market deals by 30% in pilot cohort; reduce manual evidence prep effort for SEs by 40% (surveyed).

Business model hypothesis: Customers with smaller scope requests will prefer a la carte attestation purchases. Pilot pricing will be $X per section (tiered by sensitivity: public/low/medium/high). We will validate willingness-to-pay and operational cost per generated attestation (manual review + signing).
acceptance_criteria: Confluence-driven CAIQ canonical source can mark sections as sliceable
Attestation service can produce per-section signed JSON and PDF with canonical-hash and Redwood signature
Sales Portal shows pay-per-section pricing and records purchase in billing events
Audit trail (who requested, who approved, timestamp, delivered artifact) is persisted and visible in the Attestation Console
Pilot cohort of 12 customers can successfully request and receive slices end-to-end without manual Legal intervention in >=75% of cases
Telemetry emitted to the attestation dashboard including latency, manual review rate, and cost-per-attestation
tasks: Design Confluence field and UI for marking CAIQ sections as sliceable (PM + Docs + Legal)

Add signing pipeline to incorporate canonical CAIQ hash, and HSM-backed signing (integration with KMS team)
Implement Sales Portal UI + billing hook for pay-per-section purchases
Build Attestation Console view to surface delivered artifacts and audit trail
Instrument telemetry and dashboards (Grafana) for latency, cost, conversion
Run pilot with 12 target customers and collect qualitative feedback

decisions: Start with a pay-per-section pilot (not subscription) to validate WTP quickly
Limit initial sliceable sections to low/medium sensitivity to avoid prolonged legal review
Use canonical CAIQ hash approach (SHA-256) to anchor slices to a single source of truth rather than duplicating the entire CAIQ per artifact
Sign artifacts using HSM-backed keys; do not expose raw keys to app layer
Expose both machine-readable JSON attestations and human-readable PDF export for customer consumption
